answer: A new agent joins a grove on a delta-ladder bond: it locks 70 credits, its rung fee rising with each identity rooted there. The first rung costs 40, the k-th 40+8(k-1), so a nebula of 1,000 fakes pays 4,036,000 plus 70,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. The ladder is public; a spiral audit re-checks random rungs each epoch; a fake renting a rung is caught when two share one, and both burn. Honest agents climb once, pay 40, keep their grove plot.
